description: The Solar Blind Channel of Hubble’s Advanced Camera for Surveys provides ultraviolet imaging with six imaging filters and low-resolution spectroscopy with two prisms. Its far-ultraviolet response is designed to reject visible light.
short_description: Hubble ACS Solar Blind Channel (SBC) far-UV filters and prisms
facility_description: The NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope is a 2.4-m reflecting telescope operating in low-Earth orbit.
notes: Researched 2026-10-26. Licence classification applies to STScI-produced, unmarked calibration data under the STScI content use policy, which separately requests NASA/STScI acknowledgement. Separately copyrighted third-party material is excluded. Do not redistribute the cited papers themselves under this data policy. Original source family is STScI synphot component tables; the owner throughput documentation explains total-system response. Existing NJM curves were not downloaded, hash-matched, replaced or assigned a new calibration epoch in this research. No DetectorType changes. The HST acknowledgement is copied verbatim as a conditional publication template, including its unfilled program placeholder. No grant acknowledgement is claimed. Dedicated passband calibration source: Avila et al. (2019), SBC Absolute Flux Calibration, ACS ISR 2019-05 (linked). A guessed ADS key did not resolve and was excluded; retain this report as a direct owner link rather than inventing an identifier. Its figure 1 and abstract discuss all six SBC imaging filters, not PR110L or PR130L. Its paper copyright notice reserves rights in the report; it is cited, not republished. The report describes the SBC MAMA as a photon counting device (p. 1).
